fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Self-Scoring Questionnaire
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds each of these from a plain-English prompt, and a follow-up prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_1:
Statements written around your topic

Name the attitude or experience you want to measure and who answers. Emergent drafts the statements, groups them into scales, and rewrites any single statement on request.
fields.feature_2:
Your points, your labels

Choose 5 or 7 points and the words on each, such as Strongly disagree through Strongly agree, or Never through Always. Every statement in one scale shares the same labels.
fields.feature_3:
Reverse scoring set per statement

Mark the statements worded against the scale. The questionnaire scores those the other way round before it adds the total, so nobody has to fix that column later in a spreadsheet.
fields.feature_4:
One statement per screen

Respondents on a phone see a single statement at a time and tap one label to answer it. The next statement follows at once, and the last screen confirms the response was saved.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts on the answers you name

Pick the answers that need a person, such as a 1 or 2 on any statement, and who should hear. That person gets a Slack, email or in-app alert with the response attached.
fields.feature_6:
No response cap, and data you own

Emergent puts no cap on survey responses, and each answer lands in a database you own. On paid plans, export the full code to GitHub and run the next round from your own copy.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Likert Questionnaires, Scored Four Ways
fields.tab_content_1:
Two negative statements, flipped before the sum

Corbel Logistics asks 240 warehouse staff to rate 4 workload statements on a 5-point agree scale. Two are worded negatively, such as "I skip breaks to keep up". The questionnaire scores those as 6 minus the answer, then adds all 4 into a total out of 20. Lena Ruiz's total is 15, and 186 of the 240 have answered.
fields.tab_content_2:
MAT 140 falls short of the 6 in 10 line

Halden Community College ends every course with 5 statements rated 1 to 5. The report skips the average and counts students who answer 4 or 5. On "Feedback came back in time", 51 of 96 students in MAT 140 agree. Any course where fewer than 6 in 10 agree goes to its department chair, here the math chair.
fields.tab_content_3:
A Disagree after spin class reaches the manager

Members of Ridgeway Fitness answer 3 statements on their phones after each class, one per screen. An answer of 1 or 2 emails the studio manager, Marcus Hale, with the member's comment. After Tuesday's spin class, Ana Petrov picked Disagree on "Class began on time" and wrote that it began 15 minutes late.
fields.tab_content_4:
Useful feedback climbs 26 points in six months

Ashgrove Credit Union asks its 120 staff the same 6 statements in March and in September, with a manager feedback course in between. In March, 46 of them agree that "My manager gives me useful feedback". In September, 77 do. The 26-point change posts to #people-team, with the rest of the results below it.

fields.howto_title: How to Write a Likert Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a Likert questionnaire with clear statements and totals that add up the way you planned.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Keep each statement to one idea
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Word some statements the other way
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the attitude or experience behind each scale, such as workload or trust in a manager, and who will answer. A statement that does not speak to it belongs in another scale. Lead your prompt with that line, and Emergent drafts statements to fit.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Keep each statement short and in the first person: "I can finish my work on time." A respondent should be able to agree or disagree with it exactly as written. Avoid jargon and double negatives, and read every statement aloud before it goes in.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Split any statement that joins two ideas with "and", such as "My manager is fair and easy to reach." Pew Research Center calls questions that ask respondents to evaluate more than one concept double-barreled. Ask about fairness in one statement and access in another.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Phrase some statements negatively and mark them for reverse scoring. Pew Research Center reports that less educated and less informed respondents have a greater tendency to agree with agree-disagree statements, and mixed wording balances that pull.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give each point a word, not only a number, and keep the same labels in the same order for every statement in a scale. Use 5 points for a quick check-in and 7 when you need finer steps between agree and disagree.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the draft to 5 people from the group and ask what each statement means to them. In Pew Research Center's words, pretesting is an essential step in the questionnaire design process. Then submit test answers and check that flipped statements and totals score right.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Report the spread, then the score
fields.howto_step_7_des: Show each statement as the share who chose the top 2 points, next to the count for every label. A single Likert item is ordinal, and a mean of 3.0 can hide a room split between 1s and 5s. Save averages and sums for whole-scale totals.

faq_plan.q: What is a Likert type questionnaire?
faq_plan.ref: What is a Likert type questionnaire?

prov.original: What is a Likert type questionnaire?

faq_plan.a: A Likert type questionnaire, or Likert questionnaire, is a set of statements that each respondent rates on an ordered scale, such as five steps between Strongly disagree and Strongly agree. Each statement is a Likert item: a statement the respondent is asked to evaluate by giving it a value. The format is named after its inventor, American social psychologist Rensis Likert.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a Likert questionnaire?
faq_plan.ref: how do i create a likert questionnaire in moodle
faq_plan.a: Describe what each scale measures, who answers, and which statements score in reverse. Emergent's AI survey builder drafts the statements and labels from that prompt and saves every answer to a database you own. To change a statement or a label later, send a follow-up prompt.

faq_plan.q: What is a Likert scale questionnaire?
faq_plan.ref: What is a Likert scale questionnaire?

prov.original: What is a Likert scale questionnaire?

faq_plan.a: A Likert scale questionnaire groups several statements on one topic into a scale and turns the answers into one score per person. A Likert scale can be scored as the simple sum or average of its item scores, according to Wikipedia. Four statements rated 1 to 5, for example, give a total between 4 and 20.

faq_plan.q: What does a sample of a Likert questionnaire look like?
faq_plan.a: A sample of a Likert questionnaire on customer support could hold 3 statements, each rated on the same agree scale. The first reads "My issue was solved on the first contact". The second reads "The agent understood my problem". The third reads "I would contact support again". The same layout fits a brand awareness survey.

faq_plan.q: What is an example of a Likert scale questionnaire for employees?
faq_plan.a: One example of a Likert scale questionnaire for employees rates statements 1 to 5, such as "I know what is expected of me at work" and "I have the tools to do my job well". A statement like "I feel rushed during my shift" scores in reverse. Built on Emergent, each response is stored in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Where can I find a Likert scale questionnaire sample for students?
faq_plan.a: Use this Likert scale questionnaire sample for a course evaluation, rated 1 to 5. Students react to "The course goals were clear" and "The workload matched the credit hours". Add "I would recommend this course" and one open question on what the instructor should keep or change.

faq_plan.q: Is a Likert survey template worth using?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you rewrite it for your group. A Likert survey template gives you a label set and a layout, but the statements still have to fit what you measure. A template written for a needs assessment survey rates services rather than attitudes. Swap those items before you send it.

faq_plan.q: What are examples of Likert scale questionnaire response options?
faq_plan.a: Pick the options to match what the statement asks about. Examples of Likert scale questionnaire options include agreement (Strongly disagree to Strongly agree), frequency (Never to Always), satisfaction (Very dissatisfied to Very satisfied), and importance (Not at all important to Extremely important). A behavior takes frequency, and an opinion takes agreement.

faq_plan.q: What should a Likert questionnaire template include?
faq_plan.a: A Likert questionnaire template should include a one-line instruction, statements grouped by scale, a word label on every point, a mark on each statement scored in reverse, and an optional comment box. Write the scoring rule beside each scale. Emergent builds the questionnaire from a prompt that states those rules.

faq_plan.q: What is the best way to do a Likert questionnaire analysis?
faq_plan.a: The best way to run a Likert questionnaire analysis starts with each item: count how many people chose each label and look at the spread before any average. Then flip the reverse-scored items, add each scale into a total, and compare totals across groups or rounds. An onboarding survey sent at 30 and 90 days, for example, shows whether a new hire's scores move.

plan.angle: The top 10 is definitions (Wikipedia, Simply Psychology, Qualtrics, an MDPI paper), sample anchor lists (Iowa State PDF, SmartSurvey), one SurveyMonkey template, a video and an LMS help page. They define the item and list response labels, then leave scoring to the reader: flipping negative statements, adding items into a scale score, and reporting agreement shares. This page answers the definition and sample questions in the FAQ, and shows four Likert questionnaires built from a prompt that score themselves: a workload scale with flipped statements, a course evaluation reported as agreement shares, a phone check-in after a fitness class that emails the manager on low answers, and the same statements asked twice to measure a change.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Likert Questionnaire That Totals Its Own Scores'; hero 'Get a Likert questionnaire that scores every answer, flips negative statements, and saves the data in a database you own.' covers the whole job; how-to description 'Seven steps to a Likert questionnaire with clear statements and totals that add up the way you planned.'

intent.evidence: Top 10 are definitions (Wikipedia, Simply Psychology), example sets and templates: the page defines the questionnaire and the Likert item, gives sample statements for customers, employees and students, response-option sets, template contents, an analysis method and a 7-step writing guide, plus 4 worked examples as promised in the meta.

specificity.evidence: Likert-specific mechanics: 'scores those as 6 minus the answer, then adds all 4 into a total out of 20'; 'counts students who answer 4 or 5'; 'A single Likert item is ordinal, and a mean of 3.0 can hide a room split between 1s and 5s.'

openers.evidence: Bodies open on full sentences, e.g. 'Corbel Logistics asks 240 warehouse staff to rate 4 workload statements on a 5-point agree scale.'

craft.evidence: No blocking craft defect; one ', so' ending (feature_3) within the limit; a tacked-on link sentence in FAQ 4 and a dangling modifier in FAQ 5 noted.

voice.evidence: Reads like a survey practitioner: 'Send the draft to 5 people from the group and ask what each statement means to them.'

truth.evidence: Emergent sentences map to claims_used (prompt-build, database-owned, conversational, alerts, no-caps, code-export). Third-party facts match quoted domain_sources spans: Rensis Likert as inventor, Likert item definition, sum or average scoring, single item ordinal, balanced keying vs acquiescence, Pew on less educated respondents agreeing, pretesting, double-barreled. Numbers add up: 4+2+5+4=15 of 20; 51/96=53% < 60%; 46/120=38%, 77/120=64%, +26 points.

distinct.evidence: Scoring-led angle (reverse scoring, top-2 share, before/after) is its own; no sibling primary in a heading; siblings are only linked from FAQ answers.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions; items 1 and 3 are verbatim AlsoAsked ('What is a Likert type questionnaire?', 'What is a Likert scale questionnaire?'); reworded Semrush items keep their head phrases ('sample of likert questionnaire', 'likert survey template', 'likert questionnaire analysis'); each answered in the first sentence; hub link in item 2; no brand in any question.
